problems.inputHint: Return a 4-element string array representing the four call outcomes in order.
problems.checkpointHint: Check whether a receiver precedes the dot at the call site, and whether `.bind()` has already locked the receiver.

visibleTests.name: returns a 4-element array of strings
first element reflects implicit method call

steps.explain: Call 1 (`collector.readService()`) uses implicit binding, so `this` is `collector` and returns `"auth-api"`.
Call 2 (`.call(override)`) uses explicit binding, overriding `collector` with `override` to return `"billing-api"`.
Call 3 (`detached()`) has no receiver at the call site; in strict mode `this` is `undefined`, throwing `TypeError`.
Call 4 (`locked.call(override)`) cannot override `.bind(collector)`, so `this` remains `collector` and returns `"auth-api"`.

problems.fingerprint: default-binding-strict-undefined|direct|"use strict"; const collector = { service: "auth-api", readService() { return this.service; }, }; const override = { service: "billing-api" }; const detached = collector.readService; const locked = collector.readService.bind(collector); const out = []; out.push(collector.readService()); out.push(collector.readService.call(override)); try { out.push(detached()); } catch (err) { out.push(err.name); } out.push(locked.call(override)); console.log(out.join("\n"));

problems.inputHint: Return a 3-element string array matching the three formatter calls.
problems.checkpointHint: Check the enclosing function (if any) where each arrow function is defined, not the object literal.

visibleTests.name: returns 3 formatted strings
regular method call binds implicit receiver

hiddenTests.name: object-literal arrow property does not bind object as this
arrow returned from regular method captures method this

steps.explain: Call 1 (`flagConfig.formatRegular()`) is an implicit regular method call, so `this` is `flagConfig` -> `"regular:prod"`.
Call 2 (`flagConfig.formatArrow()`) is an arrow property on an object literal; its lexical `this` is the module scope (`undefined` / `{}` without `.env`), yielding `"arrow:none"`.
Call 3 (`nested()`) was created inside `flagConfig.makeNestedFormatter()`, so it lexically captured `flagConfig` as `this` -> `"nested:prod"`.

problems.fingerprint: arrow-object-literal-this|direct|"use strict"; const flagConfig = { env: "prod", formatRegular() { return "regular:" + this.env; }, formatArrow: () => "arrow:" + (this?.env ?? "none"), makeNestedFormatter() { return () => "nested:" + this.env; }, }; const nested = flagConfig.makeNestedFormatter(); console.log([flagConfig.formatRegular(), flagConfig.formatArrow(), nested()].join("\n"));

problems.prompt:
### Task
Implement `bindServiceHandlers(service, methodNames)` so a scheduler can invoke service methods as detached callbacks without losing `service` as `this`.

### Requirements
- `service` is an object (or class instance) whose prototype or own properties hold methods.
- `methodNames` is an array of method name strings.
- Return a plain object mapping each name in `methodNames` to a bound function that invokes `service[name]` with `service` as `this` and forwards all arguments and return values.
- Throw a `TypeError` if `service` is null/not an object, `methodNames` is not an array, or any `name` is not a function on `service`.
- Do not mutate `service` or `methodNames`.
problems.inputHint: Return a new plain object mapping each method name to a bound callable.
problems.checkpointHint: Verify each property is a function on the receiver before binding, and preserve all forwarded arguments.

visibleTests.name: detached bound handler preserves prototype method receiver
throws TypeError when a requested method is missing

hiddenTests.name: forwards multiple arguments and preserves return value
rejects null service or non-array methodNames
hiddenTests.testCode:
assert.throws(() => bindServiceHandlers(null, ['a']), TypeError);
assert.throws(() => bindServiceHandlers({}, 'a'), TypeError);

hiddenTests.name: two instances bound separately remain isolated

steps.explain: Validate that `service` is a non-null object and `methodNames` is an array.
For each name, check that `typeof service[name] === 'function'`; otherwise throw `TypeError`.
Store `service[name].bind(service)` on a fresh result object so detached calls keep `service` as `this`.

problems.prompt:
### Task
`InvoiceFormatter.formatBatch(items)` currently throws a `TypeError` in strict mode when formatting a batch of line items.

### Requirements
- Diagnose why `this` is lost inside the `map` callback.
- Fix `InvoiceFormatter` so `formatBatch(items)` formats every `{ sku, cents }` item using `this.currency` and `this.taxRate`, returning strings like `"USD 10.50"` (rounded to 2 decimal places after applying `1 + this.taxRate`).
- Return `[]` when `items` is empty, and do not mutate `items`.
problems.inputHint: Fix the receiver binding inside `formatBatch` without mutating the input array.
problems.checkpointHint: Inspect what `this` resolves to inside a regular `function` callback passed to `Array.prototype.map`.

visibleTests.name: formats batch items with instance currency and taxRate
visibleTests.testCode:
const fmt = new InvoiceFormatter('USD', 0.1);
assert.deepStrictEqual(fmt.formatBatch([{ sku: 'A1', cents: 1000 }]), ['USD 11.00']);

visibleTests.name: returns empty array for empty batch

hiddenTests.name: works with zero taxRate and multiple items
two formatter instances do not interfere

steps.explain: The nested `function (item)` inside `items.map(...)` creates its own dynamic `this`, which is `undefined` in strict mode.
Replace it with an arrow callback `(item) => ...` (or pass `this` as `map`'s `thisArg`) so `this` is lexically inherited from `formatBatch`.

problems.prompt:
### Task
`dispatchWebhook(targetContext, event)` is supposed to invoke `signEvent` with `targetContext` as `this` so it reads `this.signingKey` and `this.endpoint`, but it currently throws a `TypeError` because `.call(targetContext, event)` has no effect.

### Requirements
- Diagnose why `signEvent.call(targetContext, event)` fails to bind `this` to `targetContext`.
- Fix `signEvent` / `dispatchWebhook` so `dispatchWebhook(targetContext, event)` returns `"<endpoint>:<signingKey>:<event.id>"`.
- Throw a `TypeError` if `targetContext` is missing `signingKey` or `endpoint`, or if `event` has no `id`.
problems.inputHint: Fix the function definition so explicit `.call(targetContext, event)` binds `this` as intended.
problems.checkpointHint: Check whether `signEvent` is a regular function or an arrow function, and recall how `.call()` behaves on each.

visibleTests.name: signs event using targetContext endpoint and signingKey
visibleTests.testCode:
const res = dispatchWebhook({ endpoint: 'https://hooks.local', signingKey: 'k1' }, { id: 'ev-9' });
assert.strictEqual(res, 'https://hooks.local:k1:ev-9');

visibleTests.name: throws TypeError on invalid targetContext or event
visibleTests.testCode:
assert.throws(() => dispatchWebhook(null, { id: 'ev-1' }), TypeError);
assert.throws(() => dispatchWebhook({ endpoint: 'x' }, { id: 'ev-1' }), TypeError);

hiddenTests.name: switches receiver dynamically across different contexts

steps.explain: An arrow function (`const signEvent = (event) => ...`) captures `this` lexically from module scope (`undefined` in strict mode) and ignores `.call(targetContext, event)`.
Convert `signEvent` to a regular `function signEvent(event)` so `.call(targetContext, event)` dynamically binds `this` to `targetContext`.
